personas.summary: Chemically strong, assignable chapter: every SMILES validates (SN2 inversion pair, tosylate, tert-butyl cation), prose builds the 'why', sequencing is clean, 30-item bank across 14 types teaches. NOT ready as-is: one wrong-chemistry item — the SN1 racemization video is scripted on tert-butyl chloride (achiral), which cannot racemize. Fix that and it is go; remainder are high/medium improvements (no chiral SN1 example, missing Newman/decision-grid figures, ambiguous energy diagram).

location.anchor_text: producing the two mirror-image capture events. Combine into the racemic alcohol product

findings.observation: SN1 video built on tert-butyl chloride -> tert-butyl cation -> 2-methyl-2-propanol (all achiral). Learning goal is 'show why a planar cation racemizes' and storyboard scripts 'two mirror-image capture events ... racemic alcohol product'. 2-methyl-2-propanol is achiral, the cation faces are homotopic, both faces give the identical achiral product — no enantiomers, no racemate.
findings.learner_impact: Every viewer of the flagship SN1 stereochemistry video is taught a false racemization picture that must be un-taught.
findings.recommended_outcome: The racemization demonstration needs a substrate with a stereocenter at the reacting carbon; the achiral tert-butyl system can show ionization/kinetics but must not teach racemization.

location.anchor_text: Ionize, then capture: two steps and racemization

findings.observation: SN1 section titled '...and racemization' and prose correctly says a single-enantiomer substrate gives a racemic product, but the only worked assets are achiral tert-butyl species — no molecule in the SN1 material carries a stereocenter, unlike the SN2 section's (S)->(R) pair.
findings.learner_impact: SN2 gets a concrete inversion picture but SN1 racemization is only asserted; the SN1-vs-SN2 stereochem contrast (core objective) is under-supported.
findings.recommended_outcome: A concrete SN1 example on a chiral secondary/tertiary substrate that visibly produces both enantiomers.

location.anchor_text: the breaking C-H and C-X bonds must lie in the same plane and point in opposite directions, the anti-periplanar arrangement

findings.observation: E2 anti-periplanar conveyed only by prose + video; static reader assets are 2D line structures that cannot show the coplanar anti alignment or required rotation.
findings.learner_impact: The hardest, most-missed E2 idea has no dihedral-accurate representation for a learner who can't use the video.
findings.recommended_outcome: A conformationally explicit (Newman-style) representation of the anti relationship between the breaking C-H and C-X bonds.

location.anchor_text: Building the decision grid

findings.observation: Prediction nugget describes a substrate-first 'decision grid' entirely in prose; reader carries only three individual molecule structures, no actual grid/table organizing substrate x reagent x solvent/temperature into a pathway call.
findings.learner_impact: The capstone procedural objective needs a scannable reference; prose without the tabular structure raises load.
findings.recommended_outcome: A structured decision table/matrix (substrate class vs reagent/solvent/temperature -> SN2/SN1/E2/E1).

location.anchor_text: The rate-determining step has the highest transition state.

findings.observation: The SN1 reaction-coordinate question draws both transition states at identical energy (ts_1 y=2.8, ts_2 y=2.8) while the answer + hint say pick the RDS as 'the one with the highest transition state.' With equal maxima there is no single highest TS.
findings.learner_impact: A student reading the diagram literally sees a tie and cannot apply the given hint; it also models an atypical profile that muddies the standard SN1 picture.
findings.recommended_outcome: Draw the first (ionization) TS distinctly higher than the second so diagram, answer, and hint are consistent.

location.anchor_text: sodium ethoxide

findings.observation: asset id mol-sodium-methoxide-target names a reagent but its content is a product (methyl propyl ether, CCCOC); the nugget practice_check reasons about 'sodium ethoxide' while the attached asset derives from methoxide — reagent labels drift across prose, practice check, and asset id.
findings.learner_impact: Minor, but an id saying methoxide while showing an ether product alongside ethoxide prose erodes trust and complicates maintenance.
findings.recommended_outcome: Name the same species consistently across prose, practice check, and asset ids.

strengths: All 15 molecular assets validate, including stereochemistry ((S)-2-bromobutane -> (R)-2-butanol correctly encodes SN2 inversion; tosylate and tert-butyl cation correct).
Mechanistic prose consistently teaches the 'why' rather than asserting outcomes.
Concept prerequisites and section ordering are explicit and correctly sequenced.
The 30-question bank spans 14 types with correct answer keys, teaching feedback, and laddered hints.
open_questions: The E2 hotspot answers depend on the rendered atom indexing of 2-bromobutane, unverifiable from the package alone; confirm atom ids map to the intended beta carbons.
Every question has demo_eligible:false — intentional for this chapter, or should some (curved_arrow / reaction_coordinate) be surfaced as demos?

personas.summary: Prose clear and well-sequenced; question bank strong (hint ladders, targeted explanations, variants). But the reader itself works against a shaky learner: densest 'expanded' tier is the default, mechanism videos are hidden/empty, only isolated static structures (no curved arrows/TS), the promised decision grid is never drawn, and every section's Background-reading links point to non-existent Wikipedia pages. No embedded checkpoints/retrieval.

location.anchor_text: Within each family the distinction is the number of steps.

findings.observation: Reader renders the 'expanded' tier by default; the first section packs sub-vs-elim, concerted-vs-stepwise, 2nd/1st order, RDS, and nucleophile/base dual character into three paragraphs before any practice or picture.
findings.learner_impact: Rereads repeatedly, cannot tell the load-bearing idea, starts behind; many disengage before mechanisms.
findings.recommended_outcome: Gentler default entry (lighter tier or short orienting overview) introducing one distinction at a time.

location.anchor_text: those three groups swing past the plane

findings.observation: SN2/SN1/E2 sections describe motion to visualize, but mechanism videos are is_hidden:true with empty url, so no animation plays.
findings.learner_impact: A student who can't already picture backside attack has nothing to look at; guesses stereochem.
findings.recommended_outcome: The dynamic mechanism content the prose depends on must be present/visible, or an equivalent step-by-step visual must stand in.

location.anchor_text: (S)-2-bromobutane with hydroxide ... gives (R)-2-butanol

findings.observation: Only figures per mechanism are isolated static line structures of SM and product; no curved arrows, no nucleophile/base, no transition state.
findings.learner_impact: Sees bromide then alcohol but nothing showing how/where inversion happens; memorizes structures without the step.
findings.recommended_outcome: Each mechanism needs an arrow-pushing visual connecting substrate to product through the attacking species and TS/intermediate.

location.anchor_text: converts the four mechanisms into a single predictive tool

findings.observation: Capstone repeatedly promises a decision 'grid' but the reader never shows a grid/table/flowchart; the four-variable procedure exists only as dense prose.
findings.learner_impact: Asked to cross substrate/reagent/solvent/temperature with no visual scaffold; gives up or memorizes condition sets.
findings.recommended_outcome: Present the promised decision aid as an actual grid/flowchart plus one fully worked prediction walking the four inputs in order.

location.anchor_text: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_four_pathways_of_alkyl_halide_reactivity

findings.observation: Every section's 'Background reading' link is the literal concept title as a Wikipedia URL, producing pages that do not exist.
findings.learner_impact: A confused student clicking for help lands on a 'page does not exist' screen and loses trust in the chapter's resources.
findings.recommended_outcome: Background-reading links must resolve to real relevant pages or be removed.

location.anchor_text: electron pair enters the antibonding orbital

findings.observation: Mechanism prose relies on ungrounded prerequisite vocab (antibonding orbital, sp2 hybridized, heterolytically, solvation, polarizable, conjugate acid).
findings.learner_impact: Student without solid orbital background stalls at 'large lobe points away from the halogen' and accepts backside attack as an unexplained rule.
findings.recommended_outcome: Lightweight in-place plain-language glosses for the assumed orbital/bonding vocabulary at point of use.

location.anchor_text: a base removes a beta hydrogen while the halide leaves

findings.observation: 'beta hydrogen' / alpha-beta carbons used from the first paragraph without being defined.
findings.learner_impact: Reads 'beta hydrogen' as jargon, can't identify which H, guesses which carbon loses H in elimination.
findings.recommended_outcome: Explicit early definition of alpha carbon (bearing leaving group) and beta carbon/hydrogen before the term carries weight.

location.anchor_text: This inversion is the practical signature

findings.observation: Reader flow has no embedded checkpoints/summaries/retrieval; nuggets' practice_check pairs are not surfaced in the reader, and the question bank is a separate surface.
findings.learner_impact: Reads section after section with no self-test; doesn't notice being lost until much later.
findings.recommended_outcome: Low-stakes retrieval or short recap at the end of each mechanism section.

location.anchor_text: tertiary substrates so crowded that the SN2 pathway is closed

findings.observation: Classic traps (ranking SN2 by carbocation stability, protic solvent speeding SN2, auto-Zaitsev with a bulky base) are corrected only in question feedback, not called out in prose.
findings.learner_impact: Forms the natural wrong model; reading never blocks it, so it's carried into questions.
findings.recommended_outcome: Explicit 'common mistake' callouts naming the tempting wrong move and correcting it in place.

location.anchor_text: a small excess of inversion is often observed

findings.observation: The 'small excess of inversion' nuance arrives in the same paragraph as the core racemization rule.
findings.learner_impact: Unsure which fact to hold; some over-apply the exception and answer 'inversion' on SN1 items.
findings.recommended_outcome: Let racemization land first; place the partial-inversion nuance as a clearly-marked aside/advanced note.

strengths: Question bank is excellent scaffolding: three-level hint ladders + specific wrong-answer explanations.
Reader flags the highest-leverage difficulty (SN1 order is the reverse of SN2).
Same small substrate set reused across sections lowers example load.
Comparison-matrix and categorize questions give structured practice at the key contrasts.
open_questions: Are the mechanism videos intended to be unhidden in the reader, or is static-only the intended ship state? (bug vs content gap)
Does the reader UI let a student switch text tier, and which tier is default? (friendlier analogies live in standard/terse)
Are compiled question items surfaced inside the reader flow or only a separate assessment surface? (affects struggle-008)

personas.summary: Prose and static molecule figures are genuinely accessible (chemically meaningful alt text; prose fully narrates the mechanisms, so a screen-reader user has a real text equivalent even though the mechanism videos are empty/hidden). Text-based question types are operable non-visually and mostly task-focused. The serious problems are in graphical/interactive question types: four question families ship an accessible_description that hands the AT user the graded answer a sighted student must reason out (curved_arrow states source+destination; hotspot names the exact carbon; structure_scaffold states the product; synthesis_route names the azide reagent). Separately, the hotspot exposes no non-visual keyboard-selectable atom targets, and the reaction-coordinate description omits the barrier heights/TS positions a sighted student reads off the plot.

location.anchor_text: source is the hydroxide oxygen lone pair, destination is the carbon bearing bromine

findings.observation: curved_arrow asks the student to DRAW the arrow, but accessible_description states 'source is the hydroxide oxygen lone pair, destination is the carbon bearing bromine' — exactly the graded answer (expected_arrows lone_pair site 0 -> atom site 1). v2 leaks identically (cyanide carbon lone pair -> C-Br carbon).
findings.learner_impact: A screen-reader user is handed the complete solution while a sighted student reasons which site is nucleophile vs electrophile; the leak also invalidates the item for that student.
findings.recommended_outcome: The non-visual equivalent must convey the labeled sites and the task 'draw the bond-forming arrow' WITHOUT stating which site is source or destination.

location.anchor_text: Click the internal beta carbon whose hydrogen loss gives the more substituted 2-butene

findings.observation: hotspot task is to select the beta carbon giving the Zaitsev (v1)/Hofmann (v2) product; the accessible_description names the correct carbon ('internal beta carbon' -> atom_1; v2 'terminal beta carbon' -> atom_4). The prompt names the product but leaves the carbon choice to the student.
findings.learner_impact: A screen-reader user is told exactly which carbon to select, removing the regiochemical reasoning the item assesses.
findings.recommended_outcome: Identify the available beta positions neutrally and state the task, without labeling which one gives the named product.

location.anchor_text: Draw the product of 1-bromopropane reacting with sodium hydroxide by the SN2 pathway (expected: 1-propanol)

findings.observation: Both structure_scaffold questions embed the answer in the accessible_description: v1 '(expected: 1-propanol)', v2 '(expected: ethyl methyl ether)'. The task is to DRAW that product; the name is not shown to a sighted student (blank canvas + prompt).
findings.learner_impact: A screen-reader user is told the product to draw, removing the entire exercise.
findings.recommended_outcome: Strip the parenthetical answer; present the starting material, reagent, and instruction, letting the AT user reason to the product.

location.anchor_text: azide substitution, then reduction

findings.observation: synthesis_route accessible_description names 'azide' as the substitution reagent; the graded route is r_azide -> m_azide -> reduce -> m_amine, so naming azide reveals the reagent choice distinguishing the correct route from NaOEt/PBr3 distractors. The prompt discloses the general strategy but not the azide reagent.
findings.learner_impact: A screen-reader user is pointed to the specific correct nucleophile among the options, reducing the item to reagent lookup; v2 leaks identically.
findings.recommended_outcome: Describe start/target structures and the two-step substitution-then-reduction task without naming the specific graded nucleophile (azide).

location.anchor_text: molecule_smiles CCC(Br)C, select_count one

findings.observation: hotspot student_config provides only molecule_smiles and select_count with no enumerated labeled atom targets, while answer_key references opaque ids [redacted]. Unlike curved_arrow (which ships labeled 'sites'), hotspot gives no non-visual mapping from atom ids to identifiable positions. Absent a renderer-level keyboard atom picker, a non-pointer/AT user cannot locate/select the required carbon except via the answer-leaking description.
findings.learner_impact: Learners who cannot use a fine pointer or cannot see the structure have no exposed labeled way to select an atom — the required hotspot activity is not completable except by being told the answer.
findings.recommended_outcome: The hotspot activity needs a non-visual keyboard-operable way to enumerate and select candidate atoms (labeled targets equivalent to curved_arrow 'sites'), or an equivalent non-pointer alternative.

location.anchor_text: reactants rise over a first barrier to a carbocation intermediate, then over a second barrier to product

findings.observation: reaction_coordinate description conveys the two-barrier shape but omits the relative energies/positions a sighted student reads off the plot (TS heights, intermediate/product heights, TS x-positions) that let one decide the RDS and early/late TS character (the asked ts_character).
findings.learner_impact: A screen-reader user is asked for rate_determining_step and ts_character but not given the barrier heights/TS positions a sighted student uses, so cannot derive the answer on equal footing.
findings.recommended_outcome: Expose the profile's relative energies and horizontal positions as a structured readout so the AT user can reason to RDS and TS character — without stating the verdicts.

location.anchor_text: url empty, is_hidden true

findings.observation: The three mechanism videos compile as blocks with empty url and is_hidden true; their 'description' carries only the first storyboard frame, not captions/audio description/transcript of the motion. Because hidden/unproduced, no learner sees them yet (no disparity now); risk is un-hiding them without captions and an audio-described transcript.
findings.learner_impact: As shipped, none (hidden for everyone). If surfaced later, deaf/HoH and blind learners would lack captions and a description of the meaningful motion.
findings.recommended_outcome: Before these videos are surfaced they need captions and a transcript/audio description conveying start/end states and what the motion teaches — not just the opening frame.

strengths: Every molecule block carries chemically substantive alt text (name + load-bearing structural feature), and stereochemistry molecules name their R/S and inversion relationship.
Mechanistic content is fully carried in prose, giving screen-reader users a real text equivalent independent of the unproduced videos.
Most question types are operable and answerable non-visually with task-focused (non-leaking) descriptions (categorize, comparison-matrix, select, rank, matching).
curved_arrow items expose labeled reacting 'sites' — a good keyboard/screen-reader pattern (the flaw is the leaking description, not the interaction model).
open_questions: Does the renderer provide a keyboard-operable labeled atom picker for hotspot (mapping atom_1/atom_4 to selectable targets)? If yes, access-005 downgrades to the answer-leak of access-002.
Does the reaction_coordinate renderer expose profile.control points as an accessible data table? If so, access-006 is largely mitigated.
Do structure_scaffold items offer a non-pointer input path (SMILES/text entry)?
Are the mechanism videos intended to remain hidden or be produced/surfaced? Determines whether access-007 becomes active.

personas.summary: Molecule figures are correct, labeled, and each has a learning_goal; the question bank is genuinely visual/interactive (hotspot, curved_arrow, comparison_matrix, reaction_coordinate, structure_scaffold). But the teaching reader leans on dense expanded prose + static 2D structures for ideas that are inherently spatial/relational: SN2 umbrella-flip inversion, E2 anti-periplanar alignment, SN1 two-step energy profile, and the culminating decision 'grid'. The three mechanism videos are hidden with empty URLs; the promised grid is never rendered. Nothing is a blocker; these are burden-reducing improvements.

location.anchor_text: converts the four mechanisms into a single predictive tool

findings.observation: Capstone invokes a 'grid'/'single predictive tool' (substrate x reagent x solvent x temperature -> pathway) but reader shows only dense prose + three unrelated 2D molecule blocks; the matrix is never shown.
findings.learner_impact: Learner must hold a four-input decision structure in working memory from prose alone; the many-to-many mapping is exactly what a table makes legible.
findings.recommended_outcome: The decision structure named as a 'grid' needs an at-a-glance organized comparison.

location.anchor_text: exactly as an umbrella inverts in a strong wind

findings.observation: The three storyboarded mechanism transformations appear in the reader only as hidden video blocks (empty url, is_hidden:true); nothing dynamic or sequenced replaces them, only isolated start/end 2D structures.
findings.learner_impact: Motion intuitions (umbrella inversion, attack from either face, rotate to anti) are what static structures cannot convey.
findings.recommended_outcome: The spatial/temporal transformations need a dynamic or static stepwise sequence in the reader (overlaps Accessibility).

location.anchor_text: gives (R)-2-butanol cleanly, not a racemic mixture

findings.observation: Inversion of configuration (the section's central point) is two independent flat line drawings with no shared frame/arrow/spatial cue making the handedness flip visible.
findings.learner_impact: No visual signal the product is the mirror-image configuration; could read as unrelated bromide and alcohol.
findings.recommended_outcome: The inversion relationship needs to be made perceptible rather than inferred from separate endpoints.

location.anchor_text: coplanar and anti to one another, an alignment called anti-periplanar

findings.observation: Anti-periplanar (the feature that 'most distinguishes E2') is purely spatial/conformational, but section figures are flat 2D structures that never show the dihedral alignment of the breaking C-H and C-X bonds.
findings.learner_impact: Learner cannot see what anti-periplanar looks like or why rotation is needed — the constraint governing whether elimination can occur is left to verbal imagination.
findings.recommended_outcome: The anti relationship (and the rotation achieving it) needs a representation that makes it visible (e.g. Newman/conformational).

location.anchor_text: methyl greater than primary greater than secondary

findings.observation: Six molecule blocks stacked; the teaching point is the reactivity ORDER methyl>1deg>2deg>3deg but structures are equally-weighted isolated drawings conveying neither order nor increasing crowding.
findings.learner_impact: Learner sees six separate structures rather than a gradient; the ranking is carried by prose, figures don't reinforce it.
findings.recommended_outcome: The substrate series needs to read as a ranked comparison showing increasing hindrance, not a list.

location.anchor_text: four mechanisms that recur throughout organic chemistry

findings.observation: The 2x2 taxonomy (two outcomes x two step-counts = SN2/SN1/E2/E1) is prose-only; the section's lone figure (bromomethane) does not support the framework it teaches.
findings.learner_impact: Learner builds the mental map from text alone; the lone figure doesn't scaffold the four-pathway structure.
findings.recommended_outcome: The outcome x step-count framework needs a visible organizing scaffold; reconsider the bromomethane figure's purpose here.

location.anchor_text: This step is difficult and slow, and it alone determines the rate

findings.observation: Concerted-vs-stepwise (one barrier/2nd-order vs slow ionization to carbocation then fast step) is prose-only in instruction; a reaction-coordinate/energy representation appears only in assessment (ch11-sn1-energy-profile), not the teaching that precedes it.
findings.learner_impact: Students are asked to read a two-step energy profile in the question bank but the teaching sections never show one; one-hump vs two-hump shapes make RDS concrete.
findings.recommended_outcome: The step-count/RDS distinction needs a visible energetic representation in instruction, not only assessment.

location.anchor_text: The tert-butyl cation, a tertiary carbocation intermediate

findings.observation: Several structures recur across sections as near-identical flat drawings (tert-butyl bromide x3, tert-butyl cation/chloride/(E)-2-butene x2, bromomethane x2); in dense sections this repetition doesn't always carry new information.
findings.learner_impact: Repeated near-identical structures dilute the signal and pull attention from the one new idea a section adds.
findings.recommended_outcome: Trim non-informative repeats or explicitly frame them as the shared species (e.g. the common SN1/E1 carbocation).

strengths: Every molecule asset has an explicit learning_goal and consistent descriptive alt_text; structures are correct and purposefully chosen.
The question bank is strongly visual/interactive (hotspot, curved_arrow, comparison_matrix, rank_order, structure_scaffold, reaction_coordinate).
comparison_matrix and reaction-coordinate items already model the visual scaffolds the teaching prose lacks — the formats exist in the package.
open_questions: Are the three mechanism video blocks intended to be populated/un-hidden before publication? (gap vs pending asset)
Per-section external_link Wikipedia URLs don't resolve — is link integrity owned by another persona/step?
Can the reader render a true comparison table/decision matrix inline (vs stacked molecule/text blocks)? (affects least-complex fix for visual-001)

readiness_rationale: Two independent blocker classes: (1) wrong chemistry actively taught (instr-001, SN1 racemization on achiral tert-butyl chloride); (2) four graded questions leak the answer to AT users (access-001/002/003/004) and the E2 hotspot is not completable non-visually except via that leak (access-005, a required-access blocker forcing blocked). A high aggregate score cannot override these.
executive_summary: Chemically strong, well-sequenced chapter with an excellent 30-item/14-type question bank, but not publishable as-is: it teaches incorrect SN1 racemization on an achiral substrate, and four question types plus one hotspot deny some learners either the reasoning or the ability to complete a graded activity. Remaining findings (undrawn decision grid, spatial ideas shown only in prose, energy profile only in assessment with equal-height TS, dead help links) are high/medium improvements.

ranked_recommendations.need: racemization must be demonstrated on a substrate that can actually racemize (a stereocenter at the reacting carbon)
ranked_recommendations.rationale: the video exists; the fix is the substrate/script, not new infrastructure

ranked_recommendations.title: Strip leaked answers from four question accessible_descriptions
ranked_recommendations.need: the non-visual text must convey stimulus+task, not the verdict
ranked_recommendations.rationale: pure content edit; no renderer change; same rule the compile guard enforces for mechanical leaks

ranked_recommendations.title: Keyboard-operable labeled atom targets for the E2 hotspot
ranked_recommendations.need: select the beta carbon without pointer or sight
ranked_recommendations.rationale: prefer exposing labeled targets in the hotspot renderer (like curved_arrow sites) over authoring a parallel item

ranked_recommendations.title: Draw the promised decision grid
ranked_recommendations.need: an at-a-glance substrate x reagent x conditions -> pathway map
ranked_recommendations.rationale: the comparison_matrix format already exists in the package; a static table, not a new interactive

ranked_recommendations.title: Teach the SN1 energy profile, fix equal-height TS, add accessible readout
ranked_recommendations.need: the concerted-vs-stepwise contrast, taught and accessible; ts_1 must exceed ts_2 to match the highest-TS hint
ranked_recommendations.rationale: one figure with a data-table equivalent serves instruction, the equal-TS fix, and the AT readout together

ranked_recommendations.title: Static arrow-pushing SN2 figure + Newman anti-periplanar figure
ranked_recommendations.need: see the SN2 inversion and E2 anti-periplanar geometry
ranked_recommendations.rationale: static labeled figures suffice; no animation needed to convey the relationship

ranked_recommendations.title: Fix or remove dead Background-reading links
Gentler entry tier + grounded vocabulary + recaps
ranked_recommendations.need: a shaky learner needs a lighter default and defined terms

ranked_recommendations.title: Frame the reactivity series as a gradient; trim redundant repeats
ranked_recommendations.need: the steric order should read visually; redundant structures compete for attention

ranked_recommendations.title: Captions + audio description before any mechanism video ships
ranked_recommendations.need: produced videos need a non-visual equivalent

sufficient_as_is: static molecule figure alt_text (chemically substantive; keep)
mechanism prose as the non-visual equivalent of the hidden videos

disagreements.topic: energy profile: data readout vs visible diagram

positions.Accessibility Persona: structured readout of profile control points (access-006)

disagreements.resolution: not a conflict — rec-005 does both: add the diagram AND expose control points as an accessible data table

positions.Accessibility Persona: non-visual equivalent; a produced video needs captions/AD

disagreements.resolution: least-complex is a static labeled arrow-pushing sequence (rec-006) + existing prose; producing/captioning videos is optional polish, not the required fix

positions.Accessibility Persona: required activity not completable non-visually (access-005, blocker)
positions.Instructor: atom_1/atom_4 map to unverified rendered indices
